claim_verdicts.evidence: "It states that objects should have only one responsibility and that they should have only one reason to change." Also: "the single responsibility principle (SRP) applied to classes, which states that a class should only have one reason to change." (microservice-application-design.md:136)

Code block lines 18-37 matches source character-for-character.

Line 30: `return totalVnd + (totalVnd >= 2_000_000 ? 0 : 30_000);` inside TotalWithShippingVnd. Lines 20-23 are the input `if` checks in FirstProblemWith (a lines.Count cap fits there). Lines 34 and 37 only print.
20-line cap → FirstProblemWith (lines 18-25); threshold 2_000_000 → TotalWithShippingVnd (line 30); real saving → Save (33-34); SMS → Notify (36-37). All four in the one file PlaceOrderSplit.cs.

Docs support moving each responsibility into its own class: "Attempt to refactor the class by moving some of its responsibilities into new classes." and "many kinds of new behavior can be implemented as new classes, rather than by adding additional responsibility to existing classes." Keeping the sequence in Place as its own reason is a design reading consistent with the definition and stated as "can stay", not "must".

Grepped refs/dotnet-docs, refs/aspnetcore-docs, refs/efcore-docs for SRP passages; none phrases a reason to change in terms of who requests it. Heuristic only. Section 3 hedges it ("you can often spot one"), which is acceptable; summary line 5 does not hedge it — see issue.

issues.text: "a new pricing rule" as one of PlaceOrderSplit's four reasons is too broad for this code: the discount rule lives in NamingAfter (LoyaltyDiscountPercent), as the prereq lesson taught; only the shipping fee rule is in PlaceOrderSplit. Same wording in summary line 3 ("pricing").
issues.quote: a new checking rule, a new pricing rule, a new way of saving, a new way of telling the customer
issues.fix: Replace "a new pricing rule" with "a new shipping fee rule" in section 4 (and "pricing" with "the shipping fee" in summary line 3), or add: "(the discount part of pricing already lives in `NamingAfter`)".

issues.text: The notifier example implies it receives the total, but at stage-0 `Notify(int customerId)` takes only the customer id and never sees the total (prereq lesson's change 1 was exactly adding it).
issues.quote: The notifier, for example, does not need to know how the total was worked out, only what it is.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: "The notifier, for example, does not need to know how the total was worked out; today it only needs the customer id."

issues.text: Unhedged generalisation not in claims: four reasons to change do not imply four people must edit and re-test the class; the situation happens to have four requesters, but the sentence states it as a rule.
issues.quote: A class with four reasons to change is a class four people have to edit, re-read and re-test
issues.fix: Change to: "A class with four reasons to change can end up edited, re-read and re-tested by up to four different people, even when each of them cares about only one part of it."

issues.text: Summary line 5 promotes the who-asks heuristic (claim 8, hedged as "often" in section 3) to SRP's test itself; the documented test is the number of reasons to change.
issues.quote: The test is who might ask for a change, not how many lines or methods a class has.
issues.fix: Rewrite line 5 as: "SRP's test is how many reasons to change a class has — asking who might request each change helps spot them — not how many lines or methods it has."
